title: Israel Supreme Court Strikes Deals Netanyahu Major Defeat On Judicial Reforms-Here’s Why That Matters
protest_excerpt:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced criticism over a controversial judicial overhaul ... [+] last year. Getty Images
Key Facts
Netanyahu’s judicial reforms that had been passed by Israel’s Parliament last summer, a law that had sparked protests across the country. That law bars judges from using the legal standard of “reasonableness” to overrule government decisions, a legal standard used in other judicial systems, including in Canada and the U.K., and that had been used for decades in Israel. In its ruling, the court argued the law would impose a “severe and unprecedented blow to the core characteristics” of Israel “as a democratic state,” CNN reported.

Many also argued the political turmoil over the reforms also distracted Israeli officials ahead of Hamas’ Oct. 7 attack, an unprecedented military assault that penetrated Israel’s vaunted defense system and killed an estimated 1,200 people in Israel, prompting Netanyahu to declare war on Hamas. Ian Bremmer, the president and founder of the consulting firm the Eurasia Group told CNBC in October he believes the turmoil “clearly distracted Israeli intelligence” and the IDF, while The Atlantic’s Anne Applebaum speculated Netanyahu’s response to protests could “may even have been one of the reasons Hamas dared to launch its attack.”
Chief Critics
Some of those concerns came from the Supreme Court itself, including from Esther Hayut, the court’s former president, who asked during arguments in September if the “court were barred from using the reasonable standard” then “who ensures that they do indeed act reasonably?” (Hayut retired from the court in October). Netanyahu’s reforms also faced many international critics—including President Joe Biden—who called them undemocratic, and within Israel, his minister of defense Yoav Gallant has also chastised the reforms, while Benny Gantz, the leader of Israel’s National Unity opposition party, led protests against the plan last year. Biden criticized the measure last March, telling reporters he hopes Netanyahu “walks away” from the reform package, and told the New York Times that “building consensus for fundamental changes is really important to ensure that the people buy into them so they can be sustained.” Netanyahu struck back at Biden, saying Israel—a longtime ally of the U.S.—is a “sovereign country which makes its decisions by the will of its people and not based on pressures from abroad.”
Key Background
Under the “reasonableness” standard, the court had been able to deem a law passed by parliament as “unreasonable” if the court determined it was passed without consideration for all relevant factors, a standard Netanyahu argued was too vague and subjective. Netanyahu and his far-right ruling coalition vowed to implement the judicial reforms after Netanyahu regained power in late 2022.
